about: One rail_access topic, rail-cities, that watches the Rail Access Monitor's four starting cities (docs/enhancements/rail-access-monitor.md §2) and writes about one of them a day (docs/enhancements/dailysubject_hook.md §4). It is a complete body for the admin API's POST /topics; docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics', shows how to create it with scripts/admin_cli.py. Each city's box sits inside one 100 km UTM square, so inside one Sentinel-2 tile. adapter_config sets the four sites, their reach, the 80 s time_budget_seconds cap (Sydney's first OpenStreetMap network takes most of a minute: docs/deployment-runsheet.md, 'rail_access topics') and the rota: Sydney on Monday and Friday, Melbourne on Tuesday and Saturday, Singapore on Wednesday and Sunday, Boston on Thursday, each day as Sydney's calendar has it (rotation_timezone). Every other key takes the rail_access adapter's default (docs/enhancements/vision.md §5). The research tick measures the cities in turn, one per tick, whatever the day. The daily cycle runs every day at 09:05 Sydney time and writes about the day's city alone, from every Finding about that city since its last article on that city. findings_window_hours is 192 (8 days): Boston's 7 days between its Thursdays, the longest gap in the rota, plus a day for a clock change or a late run (the two-day cities need only 120). The window never reaches back past the city's own last article, so no Finding is drafted twice; one that reports two cities is drafted on each one's day. A day with no new Finding about its city stops before any model call. The editorial goal names no city: the day's mandate adds it. Adding a city means adding a site and giving it a day in the rota; every site needs one. force_manual_review is forced on for this adapter whether or not it is sent.

editorial_goals.primary_focus: Report what the rail access measurements show for the day's city: the share of its built-up area within walking reach of a rail station, the built-up area beyond it, the station count, the scene's capture date and coverage, and the rule-based flags and simulations, as proxies measured from satellite imagery and OpenStreetMap.
editorial_goals.exclusion_criteria: No ridership, timetable, journey time, cost or funding claims; no recommendation to build, extend or close anything; no cause, forecast, political or planning view; no comparison with a city the findings do not measure; no place names or numbers that are not in the findings.
